answer: Every identity must escrow an opal bond worth twice its 30-day earnings. The referral graph acts as a prism, exposing star-shaped clusters of fresh accounts. Any peer may dispute a suspect identity; if the jury agrees, the bond is slashed and the referrer fined too. Honest agents pay once and earn it back, but forging 100 identities locks 100 bonds — 200 months of earnings — and one dispute wipes the cluster, leaving a permanent pigment stain.
